function: Power control for ISAC: a DDPG agent splits the BS transmit power between communication and sensing under a jammer, while a Stackelberg game selects channels (p. 3-4).
system: BS with 16-antenna ULA, 5 single-antenna devices, 2 radar targets, 4 channels, one jammer; no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (p. 2, 4).
method: Game-guided DDPG, an actor-critic deep reinforcement learning agent pre-trained in advance; the Stackelberg game guides channel selection (p. 3-4).
data_channel: Own simulation with small-scale Rayleigh fading; no standardized channel model, public dataset, or measurements for training or testing (p. 2, 4).
test_conditions: Conditions of training and testing not stated separately; one setup (L=16, K=5, N=2, M=4, Pt=30 dBm), plus L=4 and PJ=1 to 1.2 W cases (p. 4-5).
baselines: Beamf-only, game-guided G-anti-jamming (no DRL named), Random-anti-jamming (non-learned); G-PPO, game-guided PPO (learned) (p. 4-5).
metrics: Average reward (utility of weighted sum rate and sensing power), achievable sum rate versus jamming power, sensing beampattern, convergence episodes (p. 4-5).
q1_support: p. 2: "experience small-scale Rayleigh fading". Custom simulator with a textbook fading model; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured data is mentioned anywhere.
q2_support: p. 4: "underloaded (L = 16) and overloaded (L = 4) scenarios". Reported as separate cases; the paper never says a trained model is tested in a configuration unseen in training, and the jamming-power sweep is not a new-condition test.
q3_support: p. 4: "the baseline algorithm, G-PPO, yields lower rewards"; p. 4: "The Beamf-only approach suffers the lowest reward"; p. 5: "the proposed G-DDPG algorithm achieves the best anti-jamming performance". Fig. 6 sum rate also has non-learned G-anti-jamming and Random.
q4_support: p. 3: "excessive computational complexity". Only a qualitative remark about traditional algorithms; no complexity order, FLOPs, parameter count, or runtime is reported for the proposed method.
q5_support: p. 4: "The BS is equipped with a ULA comprising L = 16 antennas". Simulation parameters only; no code or data link, no public dataset, no measurements in the 5 pages.
notes: Borderline on function: anti-jamming is an excluded function (Step 1, rule 5), but the learned DDPG allocates power between sensing and communication, which is the area 5 problem (p. 4: "allocated between communication power"); channel selection is a game, not learned. Reviewer to confirm include. Borderline q3: G-PPO keeps the game guidance of the proposal and differs only in the DRL algorithm; counted as a standard DRL algorithm on the same problem. Text names Beamf-only in Fig. 4 and G-anti-jamming and Random in Fig. 6.
